observations.claim: IT is 2 people for 140 staff carrying devices, access, the file estate, TMS admin and everything AI; the manager describes himself as living in the backlog.
observations.quote: Two of us, me and one engineer, for 140 people.

scale.held_by: concentrated on the IT manager and one engineer

observations.claim: Tool and connector approval is an email to the IT manager with no form and no record, and AI-related requests are now arriving about weekly.
observations.quote: There's no form, and honestly no record beyond the email thread.

observations.claim: The assistant admin console shows spend only: no per-user or per-team usage, no activity, no connections visible (observed directly, console reviewed together).
observations.quote: Usage tab: that's spend, this month, last month. That's it.

observations.claim: AI embedded in other tools arrives via vendor updates without any decision, and no list of AI surfaces exists.
observations.quote: None of that went through any decision, it just arrived. There's no list of it anywhere.

observations.claim: The overnight carrier-rates pull runs on an analyst's laptop under his personal logins; it stops when he is away, and a week's absence led to quoting on a stale fuel surcharge.
observations.quote: the week he had it off sick, sales quoted Tuesday on Friday's fuel surcharge

observations.claim: TMS permissions are coarse (everyone operational sees everything), which the IT manager names as the blocker to any assistant reading it, and the two-person team has had no clear time to work the question.
observations.stated_dependencies: I'd want that thought through per connection, and right now the thinking time doesn't exist.
